name: LT1115 (single ultralow-noise, low-distortion bipolar audio op amp)
tagline: Linear Tech's 1989 audio-optimised 0.9 nV/rtHz bipolar single, a cult pick for MC/MM phono and mic preamps, prized for monitor-like resolution.
technology: Bipolar single op amp with NPN inputs and internal compensation. The LTC macromodel header says 'extended phase compensation' and notes an input differential-mode clamp. Voltage noise is 0.9 nV/rtHz typ and 1.2 nV/rtHz max at 1 kHz, and both voltage and current noise are 100% tested. GBW is 40 MHz min. Linear Technology designed and made it, and the first data sheet is dated Dec 1989. Analog Devices has owned it since 2017.

lineage.notes: The LTC macromodel reads: 'LT1115 OP AMP MODEL, WRITTEN: 11-28-1989 ... REF. LT1115 DATA SHEET, LTC DEC 1989'. The legacy datasheet short link was http://www.linear.com/docs/1612. No second source is known. One alldatasheet entry labels the part 'Linear Integrated Systems', which is a mirror mislabel, not a second source.

The same part numbers continue under ADI, with a product page at analog.com/en/products/lt1115.html. ADI hosts the Linear-coded datasheet lt1115fa.pdf. No ADI re-spin, PCN or new datasheet revision was found (a PCN search returned nothing for the LT1115).

reputation.summary: Linear Technology's dedicated ultralow-noise audio op amp. Its datasheet called it 'the lowest noise audio operational amplifier available', which is a vendor claim from 1989. Enthusiasts have long used it in low-source-impedance stages: MC/MM phono (RIAA) preamps, MC head amps and microphone preamps. The 1990s rec.audio FAQ said the LT1028 and LT1115 'are very well received for phono preamps, head amplifiers, and microphone preamplifiers'. diyAudio members call it 'very interesting sounding' and group it with the LT1028 and LT1122. Japanese hobbyists call it the most monitor-like LT part and use it in phono-EQ builds. A srad.jp commenter said its datasheet noise equals the AD797's at about half the Mouser price. Audiokarma has a thread on LT1115 op amps. No Audio Science Review or Samuel Groner measurement was located.
sonic_descriptors: clean and quiet with low-impedance sources
typical_uses: low-noise instrumentation / measurement preamp with low source impedance
single-op-amp socket rolling in DIY gear
caveats: Single only (no dual or quad), so dual sockets need an adapter.
The only SMD version is the 16-lead wide SOIC (SW16), which has a non-standard single pinout. No SO-8 exists, and the tin-lead LT1115CSW is obsolete at Mouser.
Expensive: about 20 USD according to Frieve, against about 2.7 USD for the ADA4898-1 with similar noise.
The noise is optimised for low source impedance. With high-impedance sources, current noise (about 1.2 pA/rtHz) cancels the benefit.

The rec.audio FAQ claimed it is 'not unity gain stable', but the LTC macromodel says it is internally compensated. The minimum stable gain was not confirmed this run. With 40 MHz+ GBW, careful layout and decoupling are needed.

revision_history.changes: Search summaries give the footer of the Rev A datasheet as 'LW/TP 1102 1K REV A • PRINTED IN USA', and one summary ties it to analog.com lt1115fa.pdf. Linear's MMYY convention makes this a November 2002 Rev A printing (1K copies), which dates the current 1115fa file. The change content is not shown, and no revision-history table is visible. Medium confidence.

counterfeit_notes: No documented counterfeit analysis was found. Marketplace pages advertise bulk 'free shipping 50pcs LT1115CN8' lots. Cheap bulk lots of a part that sells for about 20 USD each through ADI channels are a red flag for remarked parts or pulls. Buy from ADI or authorised distributors. Check the Linear/ADI logo, top mark and date code, and check that measured noise (0.9 nV/rtHz typ, 1.2 max at 1 kHz) and bias current match the datasheet. No SO-8 LT1115 exists (SMD is SW16 only), so treat any 'LT1115 SO-8' offer as fake. The tin-lead LT1115CSW is obsolete at Mouser, so new-stock offers of it are probably old or recovered stock. Confidence: low.

AD797 (ADI single; a srad.jp commenter said its datasheet noise equals the LT1115's)
LME49990 (National/TI 0.9 nV/rtHz single; availability not verified)
open_questions: The print date and footer code of Rev A (1115fa) are unknown, and web summaries did not show them. Check the PDF footer and whether any 1115fb exists.

No online copy of the original Dec 1989 data sheet was confirmed. Check whether the older mirrors (datasheetcatalog, alldatasheet 70309, radiolocman di=338779, digchip) hold a pre-Rev A copy, and look in LTC databooks.

revision_chain_notes: Linear Technology LT1115 (the only maker; Analog Devices has hosted it since 2017, with no second source), oldest to newest: (1) The Dec 1989 original data sheet is cited by the LTC macromodel (written 11-28-1989). No copy has been located. (2) A possible 1990-06-01 publication of the original, unlettered edition comes from an unattributed search-summary date, probably a radiolocman mirror's metadata. Low confidence, and no copy with a visible revision has been confirmed. (3) Rev A, doc 1115fa, has the footer 'LW/TP 1102 1K REV A • PRINTED IN USA', which dates it to Nov 2002. This is the current file at analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt1115fa.pdf (medium confidence on the footer-to-file link). No Rev B, ADI-era re-issue or PCN was found. Missing links: a copy that holds the original 1989/1990 unlettered edition (candidates are the datasheetcatalog, alldatasheet 70309, 257449 (LT1115_1) and 257452, radiolocman 338779 and the datasheet4u mirrors, none with the revision shown), the exact pre-Rev A footer code, any intermediate 1990s reprint (e.g. in the 1990 or 1992 Linear Databook), and the Rev A change summary. New mirrors added this pass: alldatasheet 257449, radiolocman 525939, datasheetq and datasheetbank, all with the revision not shown.
